items.title: Jensen Huang's return, neocloud risk, and a holiday retail rally
items.summary: In this special edition of Sozzi Unleashed: At The Close, Brian Sozzi warns that investors can be right about a tech revolution and still lose a fortune, lays out three reasons Nvidia may deserve another look after Jensen Huang's return, and explains why the debt-fueled neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius still make him nervous. Former federal prosecutor Gil Soffer, head of corporate investigations at Katten, joins to discuss how Nvidia's board probe proceeds with Huang back in charge and whether he could be fired again. Brian also connects the dots on the AI build-out and inflation with a clip from Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, and makes the case for a strong holiday season for retailers with comments from Walmart CFO John David Rainey and Gap CEO Richard Dickson.

items.title: Nvidia is cheap on paper, so why won't the market buy it?
items.summary: Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including Nvidia giving back about half of its Jensen Huang rally and why a stock growing sales 60% to 70% can trade at 10 times earnings, whether the Alice Wong affair was a "hit job," and what next week's Senate testimony means for the stock.

items.title: Tariffs are back as Anthropic sinks further below its IPO price
items.summary: The 8:30 hosts Julie Hyman and Jake Conley, joined on the couch by BD8 Capital Partners CEO and CIO Barbara Doran, tackle the top stories of the day. Including the Trump administration's sweeping new Section 301 tariffs of 20% on China and dozens of other economies, in-line PCE inflation and a third-quarter GDP revision up to 4.3% that keep a December Fed hike in play, Anthropic sliding toward $78 and well below its $83 IPO price, and whether Jensen Huang is the right leader for Nvidia in a new regulatory era.

items.title: Washington Calls It a Goldilocks Economy. On a $2,071 Social Security Check, She Calls It the Annoyance Economy: Prices Up 3.7%, and Her Real Raise Is Just 3.3%
items.summary: Officials say the economy is just right, but a retiree on an average Social Security check sees a January raise shrink before it even arrives. One Medicare line item and one overlooked price index explain why she starts 2027 behind.

items.title: Apple Stock Defies AI Selloff: Is It the Market's Safe Haven?
items.summary: Apple stock is up 30.61% in 2026 while Nvidia falls 21.35%. See how low AI capex and a Gemini deal shaped the gap.

items.title: Bill Gurley: Investors Weren’t “Scrambling to Actually Own Anthropic.” That’s a Problem for Amazon and Alphabet
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAnthropic fell below its $83 IPO price on Tuesday, its fourth day of trading. Bill Gurley says few of the IPO’s buyers planned to hold the stock.

items.summary: SpaceX believes solar-powered satellites could eventually reduce the enormous energy demands of terrestrial AI infrastructure.

items.title: Pro Shop's Chad Mumm on Skins Game Return To Prime Video
items.summary: "The Farmers Insurance Skins Game" returns to Prime video this Friday for a second year in a row. This year's event features PGA tour veterans and rookies vying for chance to win $4 million at the Atlantic Field Clubs in Florida. Chad Mumm, Co-Founder and President of the golf media and commerce company Pro Shop, joined Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to discuss the revival of the iconic game and what's different this year.
